title: Let All That Breathe Jehovah Praise
description: Let All That Breathe Jehovah Praise in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 234.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let all that breathe Je-ho-vah praise, Al-might-y, all cre-a-ting Lord! Let earth and heaven his power con-fess, Brought out of noth-ing by his word.

lines: Let all that breathe Jehovah praise,
Let earth and heaven his power confess,
Brought out of nothing by his word.
He spake the word, and it was done,
His Word is his eternal Son,
And Christ the whole creation made.
Jesus, the Lord and God most high,
Maker of all mankind and me,
Me thou hast made to glorify,
To know, and love, and live to thee.
Wherefore to thee my heart I give,
(But thou must first bestow the power)
And if for thee on earth I live,
Thee I shall soon in heaven adore.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
